lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Michael, it's Pierre. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about fruit at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. My knees have been bothering me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's hard to think about goals when your body isn't cooperating.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to walk 30 minutes on 4 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Half your plate has to be vegetables. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Does your family eat salad?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just cut out the rice. That's the easiest thing.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Asked about fruit at night; never addressed
Empathic reflection linking body limits to goals
Rule stated without permission or collaboration
Adds meaning: open, but wants fit with life
Directive advice to cut rice; no permission
Reframes uncertainty as ongoing figuring out
Self-related benefit of sticking to plan
Links family to motivation; missed self-worth cue
Praises deferral as own decision; inaccurate affirmation
Explores importance of change; good follow-up
Assigns weekly goal without asking willingness
Logistics: midweek text and two-week follow-up

flags.reason: Directive rule given without permission; pattern of persuading (lines 10, 23, 25, 40).
Tells participant to cut rice as easiest step without asking; ignores stated limits.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes against participant ambivalence ('Maybe').
Self-worth change talk at line 30 went unreflected; coach moved to family.
Affirmed deferral to summer ('Maybe after the summer') as an accomplishment; reinforces sustain talk.
Prescribed 4-day vegetable goal without collaborating on fit or confidence.
Participant's fruit-at-night question was never addressed.

score.summary: Coach relied heavily on directive advice and rules (lines 10, 23, 25, 40) despite the participant's repeated ambivalence and barriers. Some good reflections and a backup-plan question were offered, but change talk such as lines 30 and 39 was not built on and the fruit question went unanswered.
strengths: Set an agenda and asked what the participant wanted to cover (line 3).
Asked permission before sharing an idea (line 12) and offered a practical, low-cost option (line 14).
Used complex reflections to capture the participant's underlying values (lines 18, 31) and asked why change mattered (line 38).
coaching_tips: Replace the rule at line 10 and the directive at line 23 with a question such as 'Would you like ideas for lunch, or would you rather decide what to try?'.
Reflect change talk in line 30 ('Feeling better about yourself keeps you going') and ask for more, rather than moving to family.
Ask before setting the weekly goal in line 40 and invite the participant to choose the amount, like 'What feels doable this week?'.
Answer the fruit-at-night question early or put it on the agenda so the participant's concern is not dropped.
Avoid affirming 'Maybe after the summer' (line 35); reflect the ambivalence instead.
